(a) During on-policy optimization, the policy evolves from a high-entropy distribution into a narrow, stable error basin. (b) Different errors share the same failure mode and become progressively reinforced during training. (c) Comparison of output diversity between DAPO and our method, with detailed description provided in Section 4.3.

Figure 5 (Left) Top-1 eigen ratio over training steps for DAPO and Ours. Our method consistently yields lower ratios at later steps, indicating less concentration on a single dominant error direction. (Right) Correlation of different logit aggregation strategies on Qwen2.5-Math-7B. Single cluster assigns all logits to one cluster; 28 and 14 use direct aggregation over all 28 layers or the last 14 layers; 28–diff and 14–diff use aggregation over layer-wise differences between adjacent logits.

Figure 2 Overview of MEDS. The process consists of three stages: (A) Logic Feature Extraction: For an input 𝑥, we sample a response ?̃? and extract a logic feature vector 𝑓 (?̃?) from the layer-wise logits of the first token 𝑦∗ in the final answer, using the latter half of the Transformer layers to capture reasoning patterns. (B) Memory-based Clustering: We maintain a per-prompt error memory 𝐺𝑥 and apply HDBSCAN to group historical responses with similar logic features. (C) Reward Shaping: For a response assigned to cluster 𝐶𝑘 , we compute a penalty min(𝛼 log(|𝐶𝑘 | + 1), 𝛽) proportional to the cluster size, and adjust the reward as 𝑟(𝑥, ?̃?) = 𝑟(𝑥, ?̃?) − penalty, which is then used to update the policy.

Figure 6 A case study. We manually annotate the reasoning structures of different responses. The responses are grouped into Cluster A containing A1 ,A2 and Cluster B containing B1 ,B2 ,B3 by our clustering method. Although A1 ,B1 and B2 produce the same incorrect answer 1342, their reasoning structures are different. A similar phenomenon can also be observed for the responses within Cluster B. We further visualize the logits using a heatmap. See Appendix C for the complete case study and the corresponding logit values.
